afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 171100
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
400 AM MST Tue Nov 17 2026

.UPDATE...12Z Aviation Discussion

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A cold front passing through the region today will result in 
slightly below normal temperatures remainder of the week. 

- Scattered showers and locally gusty winds will be common today 
with dry, tranquil weather returning Wednesday. 

- Another weather system entering the region Friday will provide the 
next chance of rain focused mainly in higher terrain locations of 
Arizona.

&&

.SHORT TERM /Today through Wednesday/...
Early morning WV imagery depicts a well defined trough moving 
onshore across the western Conus with the primary vorticity center 
and main cold core progressing into central California. A strong jet 
streak has now translated onto the eastern side of the trough axis 
ensuring the bulk of vorticity forced ascent becomes focused over 
northern Arizona and Utah later today as the entire wave structure 
becomes negatively tilted. Deep southerly flow ahead of the trough 
has allowed better moisture import into the region with 8-10 g/kg 
boundary layer mixing ratios and PWATs over 1" pooling into SW 
Arizona. Modest isentropic ascent through the 300K-305K layer was 
tapping some of this moisture in the form of light showers across SE 
California, and combined with a steep cold front surging into the 
CWA, lines of scattered showers should materialize later this 
morning across south-central Arizona. Orographic influences will 
also come into play with the deep southerly flow ahead of the cold 
front producing effective moist, upslope north of Phoenix. A few 
embedded thunderstorms will also be possible (20% chance) with 
minimal instability (100-200 J/kg MLCape), and will be handicapped 
by limited midlevel lapse rates (~6 C/km). Given the rapid advance 
of the cold front and limited temporal duration of better ascent, 
models continue to exhibit good agreement showing forecast rainfall 
amounts largely staying below 0.50".

Otherwise, a period of strong, gusty winds will be likely across 
portions of SE California following the cold frontal passage. High 
resolution modeling and forecast BUFR soundings continue to 
advertise H9-H8 winds 30-40kt developing in the typical wind prone 
areas of SW imperial County. While not the optimal or classic wind 
scenario, cross-sectional model analysis of wind, omega, and 
stability suggest strong downsloping winds through mid afternoon 
with the potential for some hydraulic jumps of stronger winds inland 
towards El Centro, albeit likely very temporally limited with the 
focus closer to mountains to the west. 

The cold front will rapidly clear the forecast area by this evening 
with strong subsidence and a weakening pressure gradient in its 
wake. The overall flow pattern will become quasi-zonal Wednesday 
with H5 heights in a 572-575dm range and low level thermal profiles 
around 5C cooler than the past several days. As a result, forecast 
confidence is excellent that temperatures will hover 3F-6F below 
normal yielding a delightful autumn day. 

&&

.LONG TERM /Thursday through Monday/...    
Another pronounced trough with strong cyclonic flow will propagate 
into the western Conus from the East Pacific during the latter half 
of the week. However, trends in both operational and ensemble 
members suggest the main cold core and negative height anomalies 
even further north than previous iterations. This would place the 
jet streak only into far NW Arizona while a decaying cold front 
essentially loses definition crossing the coastal range resulting in 
little to no forcing mechanisms into the forecast area. Not 
surprisingly, modest POPs in prior forecasts have mostly been 
eliminated. However, forecast confidence is excellent that this 
trough passage will reinforce temperatures 3F-6F below normal 
through the weekend, and potentially result in the first hard freeze 
of the season for some mid-elevation locations in Gila County and 
throughout Joshua Tree NP. Some frost would also be likely in the 
more rural, sheltered river valleys over the weekend. 

Substantial ensemble spread is maintained early next week in a 
pattern characterized by northern stream blocking, but a strong 
southern stream subtropical jet and progressive flow. GEFS members 
are increasingly trending towards a deepening wave tapping better 
quality moisture over the SW Conus early next week, while the CMC 
and EPS suites are far more disparate and trending towards a lower 
amplitude, less impactful system. NBM output seems to be weighted 
more towards the majority of the EPS/CMC idea with very low POPs 
centered only over higher terrain areas. However, given the strength 
of the current El Nino episode and intensity of the subtropical jet, 
a stronger and more significant weather disturbance cannot be 
discounted.  

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1100Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
The main aviation concern during the TAF period will be the
presence of SHRA and TSRA over the region during the late
morning/early afternoon hours. VCSH may begin to develop as early
as 14Z, but the main timeframe to see activity over the terminals
will fall mainly between 17-20Z. Operational impacts will be
relatively limited, but a brief window of MVFR VIS and CIGs cannot
be ruled out in conjunction with any heavier cells that come to
fruition. However, chances of of seeing sub-VFR conditions is 20%
or less. SE winds will quickly become W'rly as the main band of 
rainfall pushes through. Forecast confidence regarding wind 
behavior this evening is low at this time, especially at KPHX, so 
subsequent TAFs may yield some slight adjustments. Outside of SHRA
activity, the lowest CIGs will be down around 5-7 kft, but those 
should gradually lift and scatter out by the back half of the 
period. 


Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH: 
Breezy conditions will be the main aviation concern during the TAF
period. W'rly gusts around 20-25 kt will be common through mid-
afternoon at KIPL before speeds gradually relax heading into the
evening. Similar conditions can be expected at KBLH, but gusts 
should subside earlier and be slightly weaker overall. Some VCSH 
may linger around the latter of these terminals through around 
14-15Z, but rainfall activity should be clear of the region beyond
that. Once cloud cover associated with a passing system pushes 
east, clear skies will be common through most of the foreast 
window. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER... 
Cooler temperatures with increased rainfall chances will enter the 
region today, though wetting rain chances will only be around 50% in 
upslope areas north and east of Phoenix. Locally gusty winds will 
affect parts of western districts, though a rapidly weakening 
pressure gradient by late afternoon will allow wind speeds to relax 
by sunset. Minimum afternoon humidity levels will mostly fall into a 
20-30% range in western districts and 30-50% across eastern 
districts. This will follow good to excellent overnight recovery of 
60-100%. Another weather system moving through the region Thursday 
and Friday will likely not produce much, if any rainfall, but will 
introduce another bout of gusty winds and reinforce cooler 
temperatures. 

&&

.HYDROLOGY...
Gila: A Flood Warning remains in effect from Painted Rock Dam 
through the Dateland area through at least the next couple days due 
to water released from the dam. Water releases remain around 3000 
cfs. This will have the potential to flood farm fields and low water 
crossings along the river downstream from the dam.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...Wind Advisory until 1 PM PST this afternoon for CAZ562-566.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...18/Benedict
LONG TERM...18
AVIATION...RW
FIRE WEATHER...18 
HYDROLOGY...Lojero
